newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Russian space probe hits over Pacific - radio.
newsitem.headline: Russian space probe hits over Pacific - radio.

text.p: A stricken Russian space probe carrying four canisters of plutonium came to Earth on Monday over the Pacific ocean, Australian radio reported.
Citing U.S. Space Command in Colorado, the Australia Broadcasting Corporation radio said the probe had landed in the Pacific Ocean. The report could not be independently verified.
A U.S. official said earlier that the probe was estimated to splash down some 500 miles (800 km) southeast of New Zealand.
U.S. National Security Council official Robert Bell told CNN that the impact zone was calculated on the last orbit the spacecraft made before re-entering the Earth's atmosphere.
He said the satellite was travelling at 17,000 miles per hour and would take only a few minutes to re-enter the atmopshere and hit the ocean.
The six-tonne Mars probe, carrying 200 grammes of plutonium in four battery-canisters, blasted off from Kazakhstan on Saturday but failed to make it into orbit around earth.
